html:
The Pamlico, called Pomouik by the English in the 1580s, were an Algonquian people of the Pamlico River on the coast of North Carolina.

Members of the Roanoke colony visited them in 1585; their neighbours included the Secotan and the Chowanoke. A smallpox epidemic in 1696 killed most of them. In the Tuscarora War of 1711 to 1715 the survivors sided with the Tuscarora against the colonists, and afterwards they were absorbed into other peoples. The Pamlico River and Pamlico Sound keep their name.
sum: The Pamlico, called Pomouik by the English in the 1580s, were an Algonquian people of the Pamlico River on the coast of North Carolina.
